feed.title: Flame: confidential transactions with Bitcoin proof-of-burn consensus

entry.title: Flame: confidential transactions with Bitcoin proof-of-burn consensus
entry.summary:
The Flame project is an innovative Bitcoin side chain that leverages a proof-of-burn consensus mechanism to provide a fully decentralized protocol. This unique approach requires nodes to continuously burn bitcoins, which serves as a protection against double-spending and aims to address the limitations found in other consensus methods like proof-of-stake, merged mining, and various proof-of-work protocols. Unlike these traditional mechanisms, Flame does not grant any special privileges to developers, miners, or validators, promoting a level playing field within its network architecture.
Flame integrates several advanced features to enhance transaction confidentiality and network efficiency. It utilizes a programmable constraint system built on Bulletproofs and Ristretto, alongside Taproot-based predicates. This setup ensures a high degree of privacy and security for transactions. Furthermore, the use of Utreexo for managing unspent outputs and a model that allows actors to lease storage space contributes to reducing the blockchain's storage requirements while maintaining scalability. These technologies are combined thoughtfully, drawing from proposals by Bitcoin developers and incorporating elements from the creator’s previous projects, Chain's TxVM and Interstellar's ZkVM.
The project aims to achieve a security model closely resembling that of Bitcoin, with the adoption strategy being purely market-driven without necessitating changes to Bitcoin's existing consensus rules. This approach could potentially influence Bitcoin economics significantly, especially concerning the demand for block space and the long-term impact on miners' rewards. For those interested in more detailed information or wanting to contribute to the ongoing development, resources and documentation can be accessed through the overview [here](https://runflame.org/flame.pdf) and the work-in-progress implementation available on [GitHub](https://github.com/runflame/flame-lib). The mainnet launch of Flame is scheduled for January 2027, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of decentralized applications and privacy-focused solutions within the cryptocurrency landscape.
